newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Beer blues batter San Miguel shares.
newsitem.headline: Beer blues batter San Miguel shares.

text.p: Shares of beer maker San Miguel have been taking a beating as investors fear its profits will be hit by a recent beer price rise and a fizzing cola war, analysts said on Wednesday.
The major blue-chip has pulled down the Philippine Stock Exchange's composite index in some of the past few sessions, and analysts said foreign investors were among the biggest sellers of the stock.
The stock's fall sent analysts scrambling back to their 1997 earnings forecasts, and the results were mixed. Some said they had downgraded their numbers while others maintained theirs.
San Miguel B, open to foreign investors, closed on Wednesday at 87 pesos, down 12.50 pesos, or 12.56 percent, from 99.50 on February 25.
Its A stock meant for local investors was at 53.50 pesos, down two pesos, or 3.60 percent, from 55.50 on February 24.
A Reuters survey of five brokerage houses on Wednesday showed three were downgrading their income projections while the other two were waiting.

"With the increase in the price of beer we see a contraction in sales volume, and with the 10 percent Coca-Cola price drop, this will mean lower profits for the company," said Gina Roa-Dipaling, analyst at Philippine Asia Equity.
A San Miguel unit bottles Coca-Cola.
Dipaling said she had reduced San Miguel's net income projection for 1997 by 5.08 percent to 5.9 billion pesos from the earlier forecast of 6.2 billion pesos.
The company's sales volume will likely decrease by eight percent from the original three percent decline, she said.
Guoco Securities said it was cutting its profits forecast to six billion, down 5.41 percent from 6.325 billion.
"The beer market is very price sensitive and the immediate impact will be lower sales," said Saturnino Mejia, research head at Guoco Securities.
San Miguel Corp has announced a one peso increase in the price of a bottle of its pale pilsen beer.

"The price increase is substantial and would mean an additional 24 pesos for one case and this could lower revenues," said Reuben Hermoso, analyst at Dharmala Securities. He said he was lowering his forecast, but had not yet arrived at a number.
The analysts said competition in the soft drinks market had intensified as competing brands have also announced price cuts.
San Miguel's soft drinks unit Coca-Cola Bottlers Philippines Inc is 70 percent owned by San Miguel and 30 percent by the Coca-Cola Company.
One analyst, however, said a price war among soft drink brands may be short- lived.

"They have done this before and it was short-term, meaning that once the company reaches the objective, they raise prices again. And, of course, the market for beer is really shrinking due to a shift in consumer taste to hard liquor," said Spencer Yap, research head at BPI Capital Corp.
Yap said he was retaining his earlier profits forecast of 6.0 billion pesos.
Jonas Ferrer, research director at Pryce Securities, took a similar view. "We just have to wait-and-see if these price issues will really squeeze the company," he said.
Pryce Securities had forecast profits at 5.4 billion.
In 1996, San Miguel reported net profit of 6.09 billion pesos.
